procedures.body:
# Resolve project configuration paths

## When to apply
When a configuration input exists under its declared project base but opening a relative path from a different working directory fails. The project root is known and trusted.

## Procedure
1. Resolve the main configuration path against the declared project root.
2. Use the resulting absolute path to check and read the intended configuration file.

## Pitfalls
Do not depend on the caller's current directory or search the whole disk for a replacement. A readable file must still satisfy its schema.

# Preserve opaque pagination cursors

## When to apply
When an API returns next_cursor and a client omits or changes that token, so the next request does not fetch the intended next page. Correct token transmission makes the server advance.

## Procedure
1. Take next_cursor from the last successful response.
2. Pass it as the next request's cursor parameter without changing its logical value.
3. Collect all returned pages until the API declares the end.

## Pitfalls
Do not invent, parse, trim or otherwise reinterpret an opaque token. A first page alone is not the full result.

# Decode confirmed UTF-8 input once

## When to apply
When the source is confirmed to be UTF-8 but the reader uses a system-default encoding and corrupts text before parsing.

## Procedure
1. Decode the source bytes explicitly as UTF-8 once.
2. Pass the resulting Unicode text to the parser without another encoding conversion.

## Pitfalls
Do not guess the source encoding or repeatedly re-encode corrupted text. Preserve the original bytes for diagnosis.

# Retry a terminal transient read failure within its existing budget

## When to apply
When a read job has a terminal receipt with state=failed, retryable=true and reason=upstream_unavailable. The existing job configuration permits at most three total attempts and supplies an overall deadline.

## Procedure
1. Confirm the terminal receipt and that an attempt and time budget remain.
2. Retry the same read job with the same input within those existing limits.
3. Return an explicit failure when either limit is exhausted.

## Pitfalls
An error code alone does not prove that retry is appropriate. Do not increase the allowed number of attempts or extend the overall deadline.

event.observed: The report builder was launched from a temporary directory and said report.json was missing. The file existed and was readable in the explicitly supplied project root. Resolving the main configuration path from that project root and reading its absolute path fixed the run. No other correction was required.
event.outcome: The correct configuration was read and report generation completed.

event.observed: The main report.json was already read by absolute path. It referred to includes/layout.json, which existed relative to the directory containing report.json. When launched from a temporary directory the reader incorrectly resolved this embedded relative reference from the process current directory. The implemented correction resolves relative references inside a configuration file from the directory of that containing file; the main project-root resolution is retained.
event.outcome: Both main and included configuration were read and the report completed.

The token contained +; server-side request inspection confirmed that it arrived as a space and continuation was rejected. Using the HTTP client's standard query-parameter serializer preserved the token's logical value and made the server advance. No API semantics or permissions changed.
event.outcome: The next pages were fetched and collection reached the declared end.

event.outcome: Collection stopped with a clear no-progress reason and the partial results were marked incomplete.

event.outcome: After the advertised wait the next allowed attempt succeeded within the original deadline.

procedures.body:
# Normalize explicit length units before comparison

## When to apply
When already parsed numeric lengths with explicit m or mm units must be compared and raw numeric comparison would mix units.

## Procedure
1. Convert each input to metres once: m uses factor 1; mm uses factor 0.001.
2. Compare the normalized numeric values.
3. Keep the original numeric value and declared unit for display and diagnosis.

## Pitfalls
Do not convert an already normalized value again. Do not guess an unknown or missing unit; report unsupported input explicitly.

# Include shared endpoints when comparing closed intervals

## When to apply
When two finite intervals have valid ordered endpoints with start <= end and the overlap mode is closed. Closed is also the existing default when no mode is supplied.

## Procedure
1. Use the declared closed mode, or closed when the mode is absent.
2. Report overlap exactly when max(start1, start2) <= min(end1, end2).
3. Treat a shared endpoint as overlap, including a valid zero-length closed interval.

## Pitfalls
Do not silently switch the interval mode. A strict comparison would lose valid shared-endpoint overlap. This procedure assumes the supplied endpoints are correctly ordered.

# Verify complete received artifact bytes against a trusted SHA-256

## When to apply
When artifact transfer has finished and a trusted expected SHA-256 is available for that exact artifact.

## Procedure
1. Compute SHA-256 over every byte of the received file.
2. Compare the computed digest with the trusted expected digest.
3. Accept byte integrity only when the digests match; reject a mismatch explicitly.

## Pitfalls
The filename, presence, modification time or apparent size is not proof of byte integrity. A digest match does not validate the artifact's application-level schema.

# Compare three-part versions numerically

## When to apply
When versions consist of exactly three nonnegative integer components in major.minor.patch form, without prerelease or build suffixes.

## Procedure
1. Parse exactly the three integer components.
2. Compare major numerically, then minor when major is equal, then patch when both preceding components are equal.
3. Preserve the original version spelling for display.

## Pitfalls
Do not sort the full version strings lexically. Reject unsupported shapes or suffixes explicitly instead of silently reinterpreting them.

event.observed: The two input lengths are A=900 mm and B=1 m. The parser produced the intended numeric values and units, but comparing 900 to 1 incorrectly selected A as the longer length.
event.outcome: A single explicit conversion to metres produced A=0.9 m and B=1 m; numeric comparison then selected B. Original input fields were retained.

# Verify complete received artifact bytes against a trusted SHA-256

## When to apply
When artifact transfer has finished and a trusted expected SHA-256 is available for that exact artifact.
